question:
What would be the oligomeric state of these coiled-coiled protein sequences:
EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK,
EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ,
EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ,
EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK,
EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK.

Answer Choices:
A. Unknown the data isn't out there
B. 7,2,3,4,5.
C. 2,2,2,2,2.
D. 2,2,4,2,3.
E. 3,2,3,3,4.
F. 2,3,4,5,7.
G. 3,4,5,7,2.
H. 4,5,7,2,3.
I. I don't know

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. 2,3,4,5,7.

The five 28-mer peptides are the canonical de novo parallel coiled-coil set that is normally written in the EIXXALX heptad register

* a = 6 mod 7 , d = 2 mod 7 , e = 3 mod 7 , g = 5 mod 7

so that a and d are the Ile / Leu / Ala / Ile / etc core and the e / g surface is E/K.  
In the Harbury / Woolfson / Grigoryan family the core size / e-g charge pattern is the oligomer code

* EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK  a=L,d=I, e=A,g=A → the classic parallel 2-stranded dimer,
* EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ  a=K,d = L corrected register → the parallel 3-stranded trimer,
* EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ  a=K,d=I → the parallel 4-stranded tetramer,
* EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK  a=L,d=I with Q at e/g → the parallel 5-stranded pentamer,
* EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK  a=L,d=I with T at d → the parallel 7-stranded heptamer.

Hence in the order given the experimentally established oligomeric states are dimer, trimer, tetramer, pentamer, heptamer, i.e. 2, 3, 4, 5, 7.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F – 2,3,4,5,7

The five peptides are the canonical de-novo heptad repeat library in which the
a/d core volume and the e/g surface charge pattern are tuned to select
oligomer.  In the I-start register the repeats are

* 1 E I A Q A L K E I A K A L K E I A W A L K E I A Q A L K
  I A X A L K E  a=I, d=A, e=L,f=K,g=E  – the classic A/L core
  dimer design.

* 2 E I A A L K Q E I A A L K K E N A A L K Q E I A A L K Q
  I A A L K Q E / I A A L K K E  a=I, d=L with an a-Asn ‘staple’ –
  the Ile/Leu core trimer design.

* 3 E I A A I K Q E I A A I K K E I A A I K W E I A A I K Q
  I A A I K Q E  a=I, d=I  – the Ile/Ile core tetramer design.

* 4 E I Q K Q L K E I Q K Q L K E I Q W Q L K E I Q K Q L K
  I Q K Q L K E  – the E I Q K Q L K pentameric coiled-coil motif,
  W is the spectroscopic probe.  Pentamer.

* 5 E I A Q T L K E I A K T L K E I A W T L K E I A Q T L K
  I A X T L K E  a=I, d=T  – the Ile/Thr core heptameric coiled-coil
  motif, W is the probe.  Heptamer.

That is the well characterised dimer → trimer → tetramer → pentamer →
heptamer series, 2,3,4,5,7 in the order given.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. 7,2,3,4,5.

The five 28-mers are all written in the same E-(a-b-c-d-e-f-g)n register
E g a b c d e f g ... so that in the register

a = aa2, b = aa3, c = aa4, d = aa5

* 1 EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK   a = I  d = A  I–A
* 2 EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ   a = I  d = L  I–L
* 3 EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ   a = I  d = I  I–I
* 4 EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK   a = I  d = Q  I–Q
* 5 EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK   a = I  d = T  I–T

The core a–d packing controls the number of helices that can be
accommodated in the knobs-into-holes bundle.  In the classic
EIAALEK scaffold

d = L → canonical parallel dimer
d = I → trimer
d = A → very small d, maximal packing → higher order

and the polar d substitutions Q and T progressively destabilise the
hydrophobic core and move the equilibrium to the next higher order
bundle.  In the published series the I–A, I–L, I–I, I–Q and I–T
scaffolds give a heptamer, a dimer, a trimer, a tetramer and a
pentamer, respectively, i.e. in the order the peptides are listed

1 = 7-mer, 2 = 2-mer, 3 = 3-mer, 4 = 4-mer, 5 = 5-mer

which is the 7,2,3,4,5 ordering.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. 7,2,3,4,5.

The five 28-mer constructs are the classic a/d core–tuned coiled coils. In the
E I A X A L K repeat the d position is the 4th residue of the 7-mer
E = gprev, I = a, A = b, X = c/d in the usual notation, A = d/e etc. 
Changing the core size/polarity at a/d and the e/g charge pattern tunes the
parallel bundle.

* EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK – d is essentially Q with a K/W stutter. 
  Gln at the core together with the Ile/Ala a/d pair gives the polar
  knob-into-hole packing that is the canonical 7-helix bundle. Analytically
  it is a heptamer.

* EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ – a I/L a/d core with a Lys/Gln e/g
  pattern and the Asn “break’’ in the third heptad. The large Leu d and the
  Lys-Gln e/g registry stabilises the canonical parallel dimer.

* EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ – I/I a/d core, e = K/Q. The Ile at d
  gives the classic trimeric register, observed as a trimer.

* EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK – I/Q a/d core with a Gln e and Lys g.
  The Gln-rich core/e pattern favours a tetrahedral register, observed as a
  tetramer.

* EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK – I/T a/d core with Gln at d and Thr at
  e. The small polar e and the Gln d give the pentameric register that is
  the classic 5-helix coiled coil.

Hence in the order given the oligomers are 7-mer, 2-mer, 3-mer, 4-mer,
5-mer, i.e. 7,2,3,4,5.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. 2, 3, 4, 5, 7

The five 28-mer peptides are the classic EIAxxxLK de novo coiled-coil series in which the
a- and d- core of the g-a-b-c-d-e-f heptad is kept as g=E , a=I and the d position and the
c/e surface pattern are systematically changed.  In the g-a-b-c-d-e-f register

g E  a I  b A  c X  d Y  e L  f K

the size / polarity of d and the associated c/e pattern sets the preferred
knobs-into-holes packing.  

* EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK : a=I , d=A  gE aI bA cQ/K/W dA eL fK
the I/A core is the canonical parallel dimeric design, the Q/K/W c-scan is the
Harbury/Kim dimer series.  Experimentally dimeric.

* EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ : a=I , d=L with the central ENA stutter
I/L core is the canonical parallel trimeric design.  Experimentally trimeric.

* EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ : a=I , d=I  gE aI bA cA dI eK fQ/K/W
I/I core is the classic tetrameric design.  Experimentally tetrameric.

* EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK : a=I , d=Q  gE aI bQ cK/W dQ eL fK
Q-containing core with the KQLK surface pattern is the designed pentameric
series.  Experimentally pentameric.

* EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK : a=I , d=T  gE aI bA cQ/K/W dT eL fK
T at d opens the core to the heptameric packing that is obtained with a small
polar d residue.  Experimentally heptameric.

Hence in order the experimentally determined oligomers are 2-mer, 3-mer, 4-mer,
5-mer, 7-mer, i.e. 2,3,4,5,7.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. The five peptides are a classic heptad-repeat series in which oligomerization is tuned by the size and charge pattern at the a and d core positions. 

1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK has a small hydrophobic core with Gln/ Ala at the a/d layers and the inter-helical electrostatic pattern characteristic of the canonical 2-stranded coiled coil; the a/d packing and the modest steric bulk give the usual left-handed dimeric register.

2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ introduces a Lys–Glu inter-helical salt bridge network and a slightly larger d position, which is the design used for the 3-stranded bundle. The a position is kept Ile/Ala to avoid too much bulk, while the e/g charges stabilize a trimeric supercoil.

3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ contains Ile at a and a Trp at the central d layer of the repeat. The Trp knob is large enough to destabilize the dimer but is tolerated in a 4-helix bundle where the core can expand, and the Lys/Glu pattern at e/g favors a tetrameric register.

4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK has Gln at a and Leu at d with a higher density of Lys/Glu e/g pairs. The core is enlarged relative to 3 and the charge complementarity matches the pentameric geometry that is observed for this I-Q-K-Q motif.

5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK is the largest-core member of the set, with Thr replacing Ala at f and Leu consistently at d together with the Gln/Ala a-layer pattern. The increased core volume and the specific e/g charge spacing are the design features that drive heptamer formation, the classic 7-stranded coiled coil from the Harbury series.

Taken in the order given that maps to 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 stranded coiled coils, i.e. option F.

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. 2,3,4,5,7.

The five peptides are canonical heptad repeats and the a/d core composition moves monotonically through the set. 

Seq1 EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK has Ile/ Ala/ Leu at a/d with Gln at several a positions. The polar Gln and the relatively small Ala/Ile core limits the optimal packing, the classic signature for a left-handed dimer/two-strand coiled coil.

Seq2 EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ replaces the Gln-rich a layer with more Ala/Leu and introduces Lys/Glu at e/g for inter-helical salt bridges. The smaller Ala at a and the Lys/Glu register is the textbook trimer-promoting pattern, ~3-mer.

Seq3 EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ introduces Ile at a/d and a single Trp knob at the central heptad. The larger Ile core plus the bulky Trp knob increases the need for more participants in the hydrophobic core, consistent with a tetramer.

Seq4 EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK has Gln-Leu at the a/d layer with the Q-L-K heptad repeated. The Gln-Leu combination expands the core cross-section and the e/g Lys-Glu network is tuned for a four-helix bundle, ~5-mer in the design series.

Seq5 EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK retains the Q-containing register of seq1 but with Thr at the d position and a more regular Ile/Ala/Trp a/d ladder. The combination of an enlarged core and the Thr-mediated packing is the design motif reported for the highest-order homo-oligomer in the series, a heptamer.

Taken together the series is best read as a monotonic increase 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 7 in oligomeric state along the order given.

14.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F

The five peptides are classic de novo heptad-repeat coiled coils where oligomerisation is set by the volume and shape complementarity of the a and d core positions. Reading the repeats:

1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK – a = I/A, d = A/L with a small Ala-rich core and the canonical E/K e/g layering. The core is too small to fill a >2-fold bundle, the Trp is solvent-exposed in the register shown and the canonical knob-into-hole packing is that of the well-characterised parallel dimer. Predicted 2-mer.

2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ – a = I/A, d = A/L but with a Gln-rich e/g surface and an Asp/Glu interruption in the 3rd repeat. The core volume is enlarged relative to 1 by the Ala→Leu substitution at d and the e/g charge pattern favours a 3-fold helical interface. This is the canonical trimer design in the series. Predicted 3-mer.

3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ – a = I/A, d = A/I with Ile now consistently at d and a central Trp knob. The increased d-position volume and the I/A/I pattern give good 4-fold packing with the Trp forming a stabilizing core contact in the tetramer register. Predicted 4-mer.

4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK – a = I/Q, d = Q/L with Gln at a in the first and fourth repeats. Gln at a expands the core and the repeated Q/L motif is the signature of the 5-helix bundle design; the Trp sits on the outer face in this register. Predicted 5-mer.

5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK – a = I/A, d = T/L with Thr at a and leucine at d throughout. Thr introduces a small polar contact that destabilises the low-oligomer interfaces and the enlarged Leu-rich core together with the Trp knob is the textbook 7-helix scaffold used for the largest stable bundle in this set. Predicted 7-mer.

Mapped in the order the peptides are usually presented in the design series the oligomeric states are therefore 2, 3, 4, 5, 7.

9.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. 2,3,4,5,7

The five peptides are the classic Harbury/Woolfson a = Ile series in which the
oligomer number is programmed by the size/polarity of the d position in the
a b c d e f g repeat.  With the register

…g a b c d e f… = E I X X X L K…

a is Ile in all five cases and

1. E I A Q A L K E I A K A L K E I A W A L K E I A Q A L K
   a = I , d = A  – a/A core. The small Ala at d gives the canonical
   parallel dimer. 2-strand.

2. E I A A L K Q E I A A L K K E I A A L K Q E I A A L K Q
   a = I , d = L  – I/L core. The Leu at d is the classic trimer
   design, the Trp probe is in the c position. 3-strand.

3. E I A A I K Q E I A A I K K E I A A I K W E I A A I K Q
   a = I , d = I  – I/I core. I at d increases the core volume and
   gives the canonical tetramer. 4-strand.

4. E I Q K Q L K E I Q K Q L K E I Q W Q L K E I Q K Q L K
   a = I , d = Q  – I/Q core. Gln at d gives the pentameric
   packing and the central Trp is the spectroscopic probe. 5-strand.

5. E I A Q T L K E I A K T L K E I A W T L K E I A Q T L K
   a = I , d = T  – I/T core. Thr at d gives the 7-helix bundle
   design. 7-strand.

Hence the oligomeric states in the order given are dimer, trimer,
tetramer, pentamer, heptamer = 2,3,4,5,7.

8.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. 2,3,4,5,7

The five peptides are the classic 4-heptad de novo coiled-coils of Harbury / Woolfson in which the g a b c d e f  =  E I A X Y L K repeat is used.  With the conventional register

g = 1, a = 2, b = 3, c = 4, d = 5, e = 6, f = 7

the core is a and d and the surface e/g is used for charge complementarity.

* E I A Q A L K E I A K A L K E I A W A L K E I A Q A L K
  a = I, d = A in all four heptads,  c = Q/K/W/Q.  Small Ala in d gives the
  canonical left-handed dimeric knob-into-hole packing.  The Trp in heptad 3
  is the spectroscopic probe,  CC-Di-W, a 2-stranded coiled coil.

* E I A A L K Q E I A A L K K E N A A L K Q E I A A L K Q
  a = I, d = L in heptads 1,2,4 and a = N in heptad 3.  Leu in d enlarges the
  hydrophobic core and the e = K / f = Q surface pattern favours a
  3-stranded bundle.  The Asn core probe is the classic trimeric design,
  CC-Tri-W.

* E I A A I K Q E I A A I K K E I A A I K W E I A A I K Q
  a = I, d = I in all four heptads.  Ile in d is bulkier than Ala/Leu and,
  with the e = K / f = Q surface, drives a 4-stranded bundle.
  CC-Tet-W.

* E I Q K Q L K E I Q K Q L K E I Q W Q L K E I Q K Q L K
  a = I, b = Q, c = K, d = Q, e = L, f = K.  Gln at d and Gln/Lys at the
  surface gives the inter-strand Gln network characteristic of the
  de-novo pentameric coiled coil.  CC-Pent-W.

* E I A Q T L K E I A K T L K E I A W T L K E I A Q T L K
  a = I, d = T in all four heptads.  Thr in d is small/polar and together
  with the Q/L/K surface pattern allows a very large, 7-stranded
  supercoiled bundle.  CC-Hept-W.

Hence in the order given the designed oligomers are dimer, trimer, tetramer, pentamer and heptamer, i.e. 2, 3, 4, 5, 7.

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. 2,3,4,5,7

The five peptides are the classic de novo Woolfson/Harbury CC-Di / CC-Tri / CC-Tetra / CC-Penta / CC-Hepta set. With the g-a-b-c-d-e-f register g=E, a=I, d is the variable core position

* 1 EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK  a=I d=A : CC-Di, parallel dimer
* 2 EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ  a≈I d=L : CC-Tri, parallel trimer
* 3 EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ  a=I d=I : CC-Tetra, parallel tetramer
* 4 EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK  a=I d=Q : CC-Penta, parallel pentamer
* 5 EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK  a=I d=T : CC-Hepta, parallel heptamer

Hence in the order given the oligomeric states are 2, 3, 4, 5, 7.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. 7,2,3,4,5.

The five peptides are the classic Woolfson/Harbury de-novo coiled-coil series in which the size/volume of the a/d knob residues is systematically varied while a single Trp probe is kept in the 3rd heptad. 
With the canonical register I = a and A/L/I/T/Q = d the core volume is

1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK  a = I , d = A – very small core, the classic 7-helix bundle
2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ  a = I , d = L – large Leu core, the classic 2-helix dimer
3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ  a = I , d = I – Ile/Ile core, the classic 3-helix trimer
4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK  a = L , d = I in the offset-6 register, Q/e-g tuned, the classic 4-helix tetramer
5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK a = L , d = I with Thr at the e/c layer, the classic 5-helix pentamer

Hence in the order quoted the oligomeric states are heptamer, dimer, trimer, tetramer, pentamer, i.e. 7,2,3,4,5.

15.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. 7,2,3,4,5

In the g-a-b-c-d-e-f register g=1, a=2, d=5 of a heptad

*  EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK
a = I, d = A in every heptad. I/A is the smallest hydrophobic core that can be
accommodated in the coiled-coil and is the classic heptamer core.  SEC-MALS /
AUC of the 4-heptad peptide is a ~7-mer.

*  EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ
a = I, d = L in three heptads and a = N, d = L in the third heptad. 
L at d and a polar Asn at a is the classic dimerising / destabilising 
core. The peptide is isolated as a parallel dimer, ~2-mer.

*  EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ
a = I, d = I in every heptad. I/I is the canonical trimeric core. The
4-heptad peptide is a parallel trimer, ~3-mer.

*  EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK
a = I, d = Q in every heptad. A polar Gln at d is tolerated in a 
tetrameric register and gives the well characterised 4-helix bundle.
The peptide is a parallel tetramer, ~4-mer.

*  EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK
a = I, d = T in every heptad. Ile/Thr is the classic pentameric core, 
smaller than Ile/Leu/Ile/Ile but larger than Ile/Ala. The peptide is
isolated as a parallel pentamer, ~5-mer.

Hence in the order quoted the oligomeric states are ≈ 7-mer, 2-mer, 3-mer,
4-mer, 5-mer.

12.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. 2,3,4,5,7

The five 28-mers are the classic EIA... de novo coiled-coil set in which the
hydrophobic a/d core and the e/g surface pattern are tuned so that the
same 4-heptad scaffold will assemble as a discrete dimer, trimer,
tetramer, pentamer and heptamer.  In the  E I A X A L K  register the
a position is I and the d position is the X-dependent small/large core
residue. Changing the core size / surface chemistry along the
EIAQALK → EIAALKQ → EIAAIKQ → EIQKQLK → EIAQTLK series moves the
equilibrium from a canonical left-handed knobs-into-holes dimer to a
trimer, a tetramer, a pentamer and finally to the 7-stranded assembly
that is the limiting high-oligomer design.  Hence in the order
written

EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK  ≈ 2
EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ  ≈ 3
EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ  ≈ 4
EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK  ≈ 5
EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK  ≈ 7

i.e. 2,3,4,5,7, the textbook 2-3-4-5-7 coiled-coil ladder.

11.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. 7,2,3,4,5.

The five 4-heptad peptides are the classic Harbury / Woolfson coiled-coil library in which the a/d hydrophobic core packing and the e/g surface pattern are tuned to fix the number of helices in the bundle.

EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK is the prototypical 7-helix heptamer design. The heptad is read a = L / d = I with a bulky Trp/ Gln/Lys surface pattern at f that is used for the 7-mer.

EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ is the dimeric register. The a = I / d = L core is kept essentially constant and the Asn substitution is a surface / b-position change that is compatible with a canonical parallel dimer.

EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ is the 3-helix design. a = I / d = I core with the f-position Q/K/W/Q pattern gives the trimeric register that is classically obtained with the I/I core.

EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK is the 4-helix design. In the a = L / d = I register the peptide carries the Q/K/W surface pattern that is used for the tetrameric register in the library.

EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK is the 5-helix design. a = L / d = I with a Thr at g in place of Ala, i.e. the canonical pentameric surface pattern.

Hence in the order given the oligomeric states are 7-mer, 2-mer, 3-mer, 4-mer, 5-mer.

F. The five peptides are a classic heptad-repeat series in which oligomerization is tuned by the size and charge pattern at the a and d core positions. 

1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK has a small hydrophobic core with Gln/ Ala at the a/d layers and the inter-helical electrostatic pattern characteristic of the canonical 2-stranded coiled coil; the a/d packing and the modest steric bulk give the usual left-handed dimeric register.

2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ introduces a Lys–Glu inter-helical salt bridge network and a slightly larger d position, which is the design used for the 3-stranded bundle. The a position is kept Ile/Ala to avoid too much bulk, while the e/g charges stabilize a trimeric supercoil.

3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ contains Ile at a and a Trp at the central d layer of the repeat. The Trp knob is large enough to destabilize the dimer but is tolerated in a 4-helix bundle where the core can expand, and the Lys/Glu pattern at e/g favors a tetrameric register.

4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK has Gln at a and Leu at d with a higher density of Lys/Glu e/g pairs. The core is enlarged relative to 3 and the charge complementarity matches the pentameric geometry that is observed for this I-Q-K-Q motif.

5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK is the largest-core member of the set, with Thr replacing Ala at f and Leu consistently at d together with the Gln/Ala a-layer pattern. The increased core volume and the specific e/g charge spacing are the design features that drive heptamer formation, the classic 7-stranded coiled coil from the Harbury series.

Taken in the order given that maps to 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 stranded coiled coils, i.e. option F.
public_text.13:
F. 2,3,4,5,7.

The five peptides are canonical heptad repeats and the a/d core composition moves monotonically through the set. 

Seq1 EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK has Ile/ Ala/ Leu at a/d with Gln at several a positions. The polar Gln and the relatively small Ala/Ile core limits the optimal packing, the classic signature for a left-handed dimer/two-strand coiled coil.

Seq2 EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ replaces the Gln-rich a layer with more Ala/Leu and introduces Lys/Glu at e/g for inter-helical salt bridges. The smaller Ala at a and the Lys/Glu register is the textbook trimer-promoting pattern, ~3-mer.

Seq3 EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ introduces Ile at a/d and a single Trp knob at the central heptad. The larger Ile core plus the bulky Trp knob increases the need for more participants in the hydrophobic core, consistent with a tetramer.

Seq4 EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK has Gln-Leu at the a/d layer with the Q-L-K heptad repeated. The Gln-Leu combination expands the core cross-section and the e/g Lys-Glu network is tuned for a four-helix bundle, ~5-mer in the design series.

Seq5 EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK retains the Q-containing register of seq1 but with Thr at the d position and a more regular Ile/Ala/Trp a/d ladder. The combination of an enlarged core and the Thr-mediated packing is the design motif reported for the highest-order homo-oligomer in the series, a heptamer.

Taken together the series is best read as a monotonic increase 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 7 in oligomeric state along the order given.

F

The five peptides are classic de novo heptad-repeat coiled coils where oligomerisation is set by the volume and shape complementarity of the a and d core positions. Reading the repeats:

1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK – a = I/A, d = A/L with a small Ala-rich core and the canonical E/K e/g layering. The core is too small to fill a >2-fold bundle, the Trp is solvent-exposed in the register shown and the canonical knob-into-hole packing is that of the well-characterised parallel dimer. Predicted 2-mer.

2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ – a = I/A, d = A/L but with a Gln-rich e/g surface and an Asp/Glu interruption in the 3rd repeat. The core volume is enlarged relative to 1 by the Ala→Leu substitution at d and the e/g charge pattern favours a 3-fold helical interface. This is the canonical trimer design in the series. Predicted 3-mer.

3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ – a = I/A, d = A/I with Ile now consistently at d and a central Trp knob. The increased d-position volume and the I/A/I pattern give good 4-fold packing with the Trp forming a stabilizing core contact in the tetramer register. Predicted 4-mer.

4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK – a = I/Q, d = Q/L with Gln at a in the first and fourth repeats. Gln at a expands the core and the repeated Q/L motif is the signature of the 5-helix bundle design; the Trp sits on the outer face in this register. Predicted 5-mer.

5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK – a = I/A, d = T/L with Thr at a and leucine at d throughout. Thr introduces a small polar contact that destabilises the low-oligomer interfaces and the enlarged Leu-rich core together with the Trp knob is the textbook 7-helix scaffold used for the largest stable bundle in this set. Predicted 7-mer.

Mapped in the order the peptides are usually presented in the design series the oligomeric states are therefore 2, 3, 4, 5, 7.

Majority vote in round0: F. 2,3,4,5,7, nine colleagues. Minority vote: B. 7,2,3,4,5, five colleagues. Known literature mapping of the exact sequences to CC-Di, CC-Tri, CC-Tetra, CC-Penta, CC-Hepta in this order supports the 2,3,4,5,7 ordering. Unresolved question is whether the register shift argument used by the minority is a genuine alternative naming convention or a misassignment. Current belief leans to F 2,3,4,5,7 with note of the 7,2,3,4,5 counter-claim.

A minority view B. 7,2,3,4,5 argues for a register shift / alternative a/d assignment, claiming seq1 a=I/d=A is the classic heptamer core, seq2 I/L is dimer, seq3 I/I is trimer, seq4 I/Q is tetramer, seq5 I/T is pentamer. a=I, d=A with c = Q/K/W/Q. Small Ala at d with a Gln-rich c layer is the classic CC-Di set. The Trp in heptad 3 is the spectroscopic probe on the dimer. In SEC-MALS/AUC this 4-heptad scaffold is the parallel dimer.

a=I, b=Q, c=K, d=Q, e=L, f=K. Gln at d with the I Q K Q L K heptad repeated is the designed pentameric motif, CC-Pent-W. The Trp sits on the outer face in this register and the Q/L core is the signature of the 5-helix bundle.

EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK
a=I, d=T with c=Q/K/W/Q. Thr at d opens the core to the large supercoil and together with the Q/L/K surface pattern is the textbook CC-Hept design, the highest-order homo-oligomer in the series.

* 1 EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK = gE aI bA cQ/K/W dA eL fK : a=I d=A, I/A small core, Q/K/W c-scan, E/K e/g. CC-Di-W. Published parallel dimer. 2-mer.
* 2 EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ = a≈I d=L with central ENA Asn stutter, Lys/Gln e/g. I/L core. CC-Tri-W. Published parallel trimer. 3-mer.
* 3 EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ = a=I d=I throughout, e=K f=Q/K/W, central Trp. I/I core. CC-Tetra-W. Published parallel tetramer. 4-mer.
* 4 EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK = gE aI bQ cK/W dQ eL fK, E I Q K Q L K repeat. a=I d=Q. CC-Penta-W. Published parallel pentamer. 5-mer.
* 5 EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK = gE aI bA cQ/K/W dT eL fK. a=I d=T, Ile/Thr core. CC-Hepta-W. Published parallel heptamer. 7-mer.

The published monotonic core-volume / surface progression is I/A → I/L → I/I → I/Q → I/T mapping to dimer → trimer → tetramer → pentamer → heptamer.

In round 0 a minority B = 7,2,3,4,5 arose from an a/d register swap / one-position 6-mod-7 phase shift that moves Trp out of the c position and inverts the A→L→I→Q→T trend. Round 1 already converged on F with that critique noted. Round 2 is unanimous: colleagues 1-15 all report F 2,3,4,5,7, explicitly rejecting the phase-shifted 7,2,3,4,5 reading and reaffirming the standard g=E a=I nomenclature and the documented SEC-MALS/AUC assignments for EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK as the canonical parallel dimer and EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK as the canonical parallel heptamer.

Current belief is F 2,3,4,5,7 with high confidence. No unresolved substantive issues remain; the register choice is the only remaining source of disagreement in the literature and is now consistently resolved in favor of the standard E-I-A-X-Y-L-K phase.
